<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We may also incur <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-process</FONT> research and development expense as we acquire assets from other parties.
Acquired <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">in-process</FONT> research and development costs that have no alternative future use are immediately expensed. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expense research and development costs as incurred. We account for nonrefundable advance payments for goods and services that will be used
in future research and development activities as expense when the service has been performed or when the goods have been received. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We are
conducting research and development activities primarily on inflammation programs. We have a research and development team that conducts antibody characterization, translational studies, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">IND-enabling</FONT>
preclinical studies, and clinical development. We conduct some of our preclinical activities internally and plan to rely on third parties, such as CROs and CMOs, for the execution of certain of our research and development activities, such as in
vivo toxicology and pharmacology studies, drug product manufacturing, and clinical trials. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expect our research and development
expenses to fluctuate for the foreseeable future as we continue to advance our product candidates. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>General and Administrative
Expense </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">General and administrative expenses consist primarily of salaries and related benefits, including stock-based compensation
for our executive, finance, legal, business development, human resource, and support functions. Other general and administrative expenses include allocated facility-related costs not otherwise included in research and development expenses, travel
expenses, transaction costs, and professional fees for auditing, tax, and legal services. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Interest Income </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest income consists primarily of interest earned on our short-term and long-term investments and is recognized when earned. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Critical Accounting Policies and Use of Estimates </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our management&#8217;s discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based on our financial statements,
which have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;). The preparation of these financial statements requires us to make judgments and estimates that affect the reported amounts of
assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities in our financial statements. We base our estimates on historical experience, known trends and events, and various other factors that are believed to
be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions. On an ongoing basis, we evaluate our judgments and estimates in light of changes in circumstances, facts, and
experience. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While our significant accounting policies are described in more detail in the notes to our financial statements appearing
elsewhere in this information statement, we believe the following accounting policies used in the preparation of our financial statements require the most significant judgments and estimates. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">114 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Research and Development Expenses </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As part of the process of preparing our financial statements, we are required to estimate research and development costs incurred during the
period, which impacts the amount of accrued expenses and prepaid balances related to such costs as of each balance sheet date. This process involves reviewing open contracts and purchase orders, communicating with our personnel and service providers
to identify services that have been performed on our behalf and estimating the level of service performed and the associated cost incurred for the service when we have not yet been invoiced or otherwise notified of the actual cost. The majority of
our service providers invoice us monthly in arrears for services performed or when contractual milestones are met. We make estimates of our accrued expenses as of each balance sheet date based on facts and circumstances known to us at that time. We
periodically confirm the accuracy of our estimates with the service providers and make adjustments if necessary. The significant estimates in our accrued research and development expenses include the costs incurred for services performed by our
vendors in connection with research and development activities for which we have not yet been invoiced. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We base our expenses related to
research and development activities on our estimates of the services received and efforts expended pursuant to quotes and contracts with vendors that conduct research and development on our behalf. The financial terms of these agreements are subject
to negotiation, vary from contract to contract and may result in uneven payment flows. There may be instances in which payments made to our vendors will exceed the level of services provided and result in a prepayment of the research and development
expense. In accruing service fees, we estimate the time period over which services will be performed and the level of effort to be expended in each period. If the actual timing of the performance of services or the level of effort varies from our
estimate, we adjust the accrual or prepaid accordingly. Advance payments for goods and services that will be used in future research and development activities are expensed when the activity has been performed or when the goods have been received
rather than when the payment is made. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although we do not expect our estimates to be materially different from amounts actually incurred,
if our estimates of the status and timing of services performed differ from the actual status and timing of services performed, it could result in us reporting amounts that are too high or too low in any particular period. To date, there have been
no material differences between our estimates of such expenses and the amounts actually incurred. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Fair Value of Stock-Based Awards
and Stock-Based Compensation Expense </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We currently have no stock-based compensation plan. However, certain of our employees are
eligible to participate in AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s stock-based compensation plans, which historically has included the granting of stock options, time based restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) and performance stock units
(&#8220;PSUs&#8221;). The fair value of the stock options granted is calculated using a Black-Scholes Merton (&#8220;Black-Scholes&#8221;) option pricing model. The fair value of market-based PSUs is calculated using a Monte Carlo pricing model. The
fair value of RSUs and the fair value of the common stock underlying RSUs and PSUs is determined using the closing price of the shares AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock on the date of grant. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For further information on recently issued accounting pronouncements, see Note 2&#8212;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies in the
accompanying notes to the combined financial statements included elsewhere in this information statement. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>JOBS Act Accounting
Election and Smaller Reporting Company Status </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The JOBS Act contains provisions that, among other things, reduce certain reporting
requirements for an &#8220;emerging growth company.&#8221; We may elect to use this extended transition period for complying with certain new </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">115 </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We may choose to rely on the other exemptions and reduced reporting requirements provided by the JOBS Act. Subject to certain conditions set

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Results of Operations&#8212;Comparison of the Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Research and Development Expenses </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Research and development expenses were $139.6&nbsp;million during the year ended December 31, 2025<B> </B>compared to $152.3&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024, a decrease of $12.7&nbsp;million. The decrease is primarily attributable to a $15.2&nbsp;million decrease in clinical expenses, a decrease of $8.6 million in outside services for manufacturing expenses,
and a $0.6&nbsp;million decrease in recruiting expenses, offset by a $10.1&nbsp;million increase in salaries and related costs, including $2.3&nbsp;million in stock compensation expense, and a $1.6&nbsp;million increase in other research and
development expenses. </P>

ended December&nbsp;31, 2024, an increase of approximately $10.6&nbsp;million. The increase is primarily due to a $5.1&nbsp;million increase in personnel costs, including stock compensation expense, a $4.5&nbsp;million increase in legal expenses, a
$1.3 million increase in other general and administrative expenses, offset by a $0.3 million decrease in market research costs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expect
that our general and administrative expenses may increase for the foreseeable future as we incur costs associated with stock compensation expense, legal, auditing and filing fees, additional insurance premiums, investor relations expenses and
general compliance and consulting expenses. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Interest Income </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest income was $12.9&nbsp;million and $17.4&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, which
primarily related to our short-term and long-term investments. The decrease in interest income is primarily due to the decrease in investment balances, as well as the timing of sales, maturities and purchases of our investments. </P>

cash management and centralized funding programs. This arrangement is not reflective of the manner in which we would have financed our operations had we been a standalone public company during the periods presented. Following the <FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Interest Rate Risk </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We hold certain financial instruments for which a change in prevailing interest rates may cause the principal amount of the marketable
securities to fluctuate. Financial instruments that potentially subject us to significant concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, short-term and long-term investments. We invest our excess cash primarily in
money market funds, commercial paper and debt instruments of financial institutions, corporations, U.S. government-sponsored agencies and the U.S. Treasury. The primary objectives of our investment activities are to ensure liquidity and to preserve
principal while at the same time maximizing the income we receive from our marketable securities without significantly increasing risk. Additionally, we established guidelines regarding approved investments and maturities of investments,

settlement in cash. Our foreign currency exposures are primarily concentrated in the euro, British pound, Australian dollar, and Canadian dollar. Both realized and unrealized gains or losses on the value of these monetary assets and liabilities are
included in the determination of net income. We do not hedge our foreign currency exchange rate risk; however, we may do so in the future. As of December&nbsp;31, 2025, we had no material accounts payable or receivable denominated in foreign
currencies, and a hypothetical 10% change in foreign currency exchange rates applicable to our business would not have had a material impact on our combined financial statements. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Board Composition </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our
business and affairs will be organized under the direction of our Board. Effective prior to the completion of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> the Board will consist of seven directors. The positions of Chief Executive Officer
and Chairman of our Board will be held by two different individuals. Daniel Faga will serve as our President and Chief Executive Officer. John Orwin will serve as Chairman of our Board. This separated structure will allow our Chief Executive Officer
to focus on our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> business while our Chairman will lead our Board in its fundamental role of providing advice to, and independent oversight of, management. Such
separation is appropriate, as it enhances the accountability of the Chief Executive Officer to the Board and strengthens the independence of the Board from management. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Board&#8217;s Role in Risk Oversight </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We believe that open communication between management and the Board is essential for effective risk management and oversight. Our Board will
meet with our Chief Executive Officer and other members of the senior management team at quarterly Board meetings, where, among other topics, they will discuss strategy and risks in the context of reports from the management team and evaluate the
risks inherent in significant transactions. While our Board is ultimately responsible for risk oversight, our board committees will assist the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities in certain areas of risk. The audit committee will
assist our Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities with respect to risk management in the areas of cybersecurity assessment and internal control over financial reporting and disclosure controls and procedures. The compensation committee
will assist our Board in assessing risks created by the incentives inherent in our compensation policies. The nominating and corporate governance committee will assist our Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities with respect to the
management of corporate, legal and regulatory risk. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Cybersecurity Risk Oversight </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Securing the information of participants in our studies, medical professionals, team members, and other third parties is important to us.
Moreover, our Board recognizes the critical importance of maintaining the trust and confidence of our investors, business partners and employees. We will adopt physical, technological, and administrative controls on data security, and will have a
defined procedure for data incident detection, containment, response, and remediation. While everyone at our company plays a part in managing these risks, oversight responsibility will be shared by our Board, our audit committee, and management.

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Director Independence </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We
have been approved to list our shares on the Exchange and the completion of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> is conditioned on shares of our common stock being accepted for listing on the Exchange. Under the rules of the
Exchange, independent directors must comprise a majority of a listed company&#8217;s Board within a specified period of the closing of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> In addition, the rules of the Exchange require that, subject
to specified exceptions, each member of a listed company&#8217;s audit, compensation and nominating and corporate governance committees be independent. Under the rules of the Exchange, a director will only qualify as an &#8220;independent
director&#8221; if, in the opinion of that company&#8217;s Board, that person does not have a relationship that would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Audit committee members must also satisfy the independence criteria set forth in Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10A-3</FONT> under the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. In order to be considered independent for purposes of Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10A-3,</FONT> a member of an audit committee of a listed company may not, other than in his or her capacity as a
member of the audit committee, the Board or any other board committee: (i)&nbsp;accept, directly or indirectly, any consulting, advisory or other compensatory fee from the listed company or any of its subsidiaries; or (ii)&nbsp;be an affiliated
person of the listed company or any of its subsidiaries. Additionally, compensation committee members must not have a relationship with the listed company that is material to the director&#8217;s ability to be independent from management in
connection with the duties of a compensation committee member. </P>

personnel, including directors, officers, employees, and other covered persons. The Insider Trading Policy will also provide that we will not transact in our own securities unless in compliance with U.S. federal and state securities laws. We believe
that our Insider Trading Policy will be reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations, and listing standards that will be applicable to us following completion of the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8212;Introduction </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a newly formed entity, we did not have any executive officers or pay any compensation during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2025. Our
named executive officers will continue to serve as executive officers of AnaptysBio, Inc. prior to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> and decisions regarding the compensation of our named executive officers prior to the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> were made by the compensation committee of the AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s board of directors. The following disclosure concerns compensation paid or earned by our named executive officers from AnaptysBio,
Inc., which may be directly relevant or indicative of the compensation such officers will receive as our named executive officers. Our named executive officers include our expected principal executive officer and our next most highly compensated
executive officer based on compensation from AnaptysBio, Inc.: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Anticipated Compensation Program Design Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We are in the process of developing an initial executive compensation program in order to attract and retain talented executives and other key
employees to lead us as a stand-alone public company. Prior to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> the AnaptysBio, Inc. compensation committee will make certain decisions regarding our compensation program design and take certain
actions regarding our executive compensation arrangements following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> Those executive compensation arrangements will be described in a subsequent amendment to this information statement. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> our Board will form our compensation committee. Following the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> our compensation committee will establish the objectives and principles for our executive compensation program and will make additional compensation decisions and actions, including ratifying or modifying
our executive compensation arrangements with our named executive officers. It is anticipated that the objectives and principles to be established by our compensation committee will be similar to the objectives and principles that AnaptysBio, Inc.
maintained for its executive compensation program in fiscal 2025, as described in this Compensation Discussion and Analysis. Specifically, it is anticipated that we will adopt the 2026 First Tracks Biotherapeutics Equity Incentive Plan and the 2026
First Tracks Biotherapeutics Employee Stock Purchase Plan, each has been filed as an exhibit to the registration statement on Form 10 of which this information statement forms a part. However, our compensation committee will review the impact of our
separation from AnaptysBio, Inc. and all aspects of compensation and make appropriate adjustments to our compensation programs and practices. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Employment Agreements and Offer Letters </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we will, or will cause a member of our group to, assume certain
employment and individual agreements with AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s. employees, including the employment agreements entered into between AnaptysBio, Inc. and our named executive officers which are discussed below. In connection with or following the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> we may amend such agreements. However, as of the date hereof, no such amendments have been determined. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AnaptysBio, Inc. has entered into executive employment agreements with each of our named executive officers. The material terms of such
AnaptysBio, Inc. agreements are described below. Except as noted below, these executive employment agreements provide for &#8220;at will&#8221; employment. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">129 </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Mr.&nbsp;Faga&#8217;s Employment Agreement </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to an employment agreement, effective as of August&nbsp;3, 2023 (the &#8220;Faga Employment Agreement,&#8221; which amends, restates
and supersedes Mr.&nbsp;Faga&#8217;s previous employment agreement dated March&nbsp;21, 2022), Mr.&nbsp;Faga serves as AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s President and Chief Executive Officer. The Faga Employment Agreement sets forth the principal terms and
conditions of his employment as AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s President and Chief Executive Officer, including his initial annual base salary and initial annual target cash bonus opportunity, which bonus may be earned based upon the achievement of
specified performance goals (and which will be prorated for his partial year of service). Mr.&nbsp;Faga&#8217;s employment is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-will</FONT> and may be terminated at any time, with or without cause. However, pursuant
to the terms of the Faga Employment Agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Faga will be entitled to severance benefits upon a qualifying termination of employment as described in &#8220;<I>&#8212;Potential Payments upon Termination or Change in Control</I>&#8221;
below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul&#8217;s Employment Agreement </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to an employment agreement effective as of July&nbsp;31, 2020, as amended and restated on April&nbsp;25, 2022 (the &#8220;Lizzul
Employment Agreement&#8221;), Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul serves as AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s Chief Medical Officer. The Lizzul Employment Agreement sets forth the principal terms and conditions of his employment, including his annual base salary, subject to
periodic review and an initial annual target cash bonus opportunity, which bonus may be earned based upon the achievement of specified performance goals. Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul&#8217;s employment is at will and may be terminated at any time, with or
without cause. However, pursuant to the terms of the Lizzul Employment Agreement, Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul will be entitled to severance benefits upon a qualifying termination of employment as described in &#8220;<I>&#8212;Potential Payments upon Termination
or Change in Control</I>&#8221; below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Potential Payments upon Termination or Change in Control </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Termination </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Faga Employment Agreement and the Lizzul Employment Agreement, in the event that Mr.&nbsp;Faga or Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul is terminated
without &#8220;cause&#8221; or resigns for &#8220;good reason&#8221; (each as defined in the applicable employment agreement), provided that each delivers a signed settlement and general release in favor of AnaptysBio, Inc. and satisfies all
conditions to make such release effective, (i)&nbsp;in the case of Mr.&nbsp;Faga, he will receive continued severance payments for 12 months, and in the case of Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul, nine months, (ii)&nbsp;and if each elects continuation coverage under
the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 (&#8220;COBRA&#8221;), AnaptysBio, Inc. will pay directly to the insurance provider of AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s group health plans, the monthly premium for such continuation coverage for
each officer and his family, for 12 months, in the case of Mr.&nbsp;Faga, and nine months, in the case of Dr.&nbsp;Lizzul, or such earlier date on which coverage with a new employer is obtained and (iii)&nbsp;in the case of Mr.&nbsp;Faga, 12
months&#8217; accelerated vesting of his AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s equity awards that vest solely based on continued service. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Change
in Control </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Faga Employment Agreement, if AnaptysBio, Inc. experiences a change of control and Mr.&nbsp;Faga is
terminated without &#8220;cause&#8221; or resigns for &#8220;good reason&#8221; (each as defined in the Faga Employment Agreement) upon the occurrence of, or within 13 months following, such change of control, and provided that Mr.&nbsp;Faga
delivers a signed settlement and general release in favor of AnaptysBio, Inc. and satisfies all conditions to make such release effective, (i)&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Faga will receive the continued severance payments and COBRA premiums described above for
eighteen months, (ii)&nbsp;a bonus payment equal to his target bonus payment for the year, (iii)&nbsp;a prorated bonus of his actual bonus for the applicable year of termination, and (iv)&nbsp;all of Mr.&nbsp;Faga&#8217;s AnaptysBio, Inc. equity
awards will vest in full (other than the 2024 PSUs, for which the AnaptysBio, Inc. board shall determine the PSUs eligible to vest based on the number of PSUs allocated to the achieved share price target (the &#8220;Eligible PSUs&#8221;) as of the
date of the change of control and such Eligible PSUs shall fully vest). </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Treatment of Outstanding Equity Awards at The Time of The&nbsp;Spin-Off </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>AnaptysBio, Inc. Options </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AnaptysBio, Inc. has previously issued options to purchase its common stock. In connection with the Spin-Off, each AnaptysBio, Inc. option will
become two options: one will be an option to acquire AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock and one an option to acquire First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock. We expect that options with respect to First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock will be
issued under the First Tracks Biotherapeutics 2026 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2026 Plan&#8221;) and that each awarded option will be subject to substantially similar conditions and restrictions as the AnaptysBio, Inc. award, including with
respect to vesting, except that references to AnaptysBio, Inc. will be adjusted to refer to First Tracks Biotherapeutics. The number of AnaptysBio, Inc. options will remain the same and the number of First Tracks Biotherapeutics options will equal
the current number of AnaptysBio, Inc. options multiplied by the distribution ratio. The existing exercise price will be allocated between the existing AnaptysBio, Inc. options and the new First Tracks Biotherapeutics options based upon the first
closing price of each of the AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock and First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock, in each case, following the Spin-Off. The AnaptysBio, Inc. options and the new First Tracks Biotherapeutics options will not be exercisable
during a period beginning on a date prior to the Spin-Off determined by AnaptysBio, Inc. in its sole discretion, and continuing until the exercise prices of the AnaptysBio, Inc. options and the new First Tracks Biotherapeutics options are determined
after the Spin-Off. Other than the split of the AnaptysBio, Inc. options and the allocation of the existing exercise price, upon issuance of the new options there will be no additional adjustment to the existing AnaptysBio, Inc. options in
connection with the Spin-Off and the terms each employee&#8217;s applicable AnaptysBio, Inc. award agreement will continue to govern the AnaptysBio, Inc. options.<B><I> </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>AnaptysBio, Inc. Restricted Stock Units </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AnaptysBio, Inc. has previously issued restricted stock units to its employees and directors, which represent unfunded, unsecured rights to
receive shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock at a future date specified in the applicable award agreement. In connection with the Spin-Off, each holder of a restricted stock unit will receive one First Tracks Biotherapeutics restricted stock unit
in respect of every one AnaptysBio, Inc. restricted stock unit owned on the record date, as adjusted to take into account the distribution ratio, and continue to be entitled to a share of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock for each AnaptysBio, Inc.
restricted stock unit in accordance with the AnaptysBio, Inc. award agreement. Each First Tracks Biotherapeutics restricted stock unit will be issued under the First Tracks Biotherapeutics 2026 Equity Incentive Plan and will be subject to
substantially similar conditions and restrictions as the AnaptysBio, Inc. award, including with respect to vesting, except that references to AnaptysBio, Inc. will be adjusted to refer to First Tracks Biotherapeutics. Except as described above,
there will be no adjustment to the existing AnaptysBio, Inc. restricted stock units in connection with the Spin-Off and the terms of each employee&#8217;s applicable award agreement will continue to govern the AnaptysBio, Inc. award. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>AnaptysBio, Inc. Performance Stock Units </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AnaptysBio, Inc. has previously issued performance stock units to its employees, which represent unfunded, unsecured rights to receive shares
of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock at a future date upon the satisfaction of the conditions specified by the applicable award agreement. In connection with the Spin-Off, AnaptysBio, Inc. performance stock units related to the $75 and $100 stock
hurdles will be cancelled and holders thereof will be granted equivalent replacement performance stock units with respect to First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock. Each replacement award will cover a number of performance stock units of First
Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock with a value equal to the value of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock covered by the cancelled award, rounded down to the nearest share. The replacement awards will be subject to substantially equivalent conditions and
restrictions as the AnaptysBio, Inc. cancelled performance stock units, except that the stock-price hurdles therein will be equitably adjusted such that each hurdle retains the same ratio from the First Tracks Biotherapeutics stock price following
the Spin-Off as related to the AnaptysBio, Inc. stock price prior to the Spin-Off, and, following the Spin-Off, performance will be measured based on the First Tracks Biotherapeutics stock price. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">133 </P>

</DIV></Center>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Additional Terms and Conditions </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">With respect to all outstanding AnaptysBio, Inc. awards (and First Tracks Biotherapeutics awards issued in connection with such awards) holders
of such awards will continue to vest so long as they remain employed by First Tracks Biotherapeutics, AnaptysBio, Inc. or affiliates of either entity. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The occurrence of the Spin-Off will not be a &#8220;change in control&#8221; for AnaptysBio, Inc. or First Tracks Biotherapeutics. Upon a
&#8220;change in control&#8221; of AnaptysBio, Inc. (as defined in AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s equity plan) following the Spin-Off, all then-outstanding AnaptysBio, Inc. equity awards will accelerate and vest. For the avoidance of doubt, the
corresponding First Tracks Biotherapeutics equity awards will not accelerate and vest upon the occurrence of a change in control of AnaptysBio, Inc. following the Spin-Off. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If AnaptysBio, Inc. declares any cash dividend following the Spin-Off, all holders of AnaptysBio, Inc. restricted stock units will be entitled
to a cash payment equal to the value of such dividend one year following the dividend payment date and subject to continued employment at AnaptysBio, Inc. or First Tracks Biotherapeutics (as applicable). If AnaptysBio, Inc. declares an extraordinary
cash dividend following the Spin-Off, all holders of AnaptysBio, Inc. options will have the exercise price of their AnaptysBio, Inc. option reduced by the value of such dividend, but not below 25% of the price of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock
following such extraordinary dividend. If the dividend value is greater than the option exercise price reduction, each applicable option holder will also be entitled to a cash payment equal to the difference between the dividend payment value and
the exercise price reduction payable (i) for vested options, as soon as reasonably practicable following the dividend date and (ii) for unvested options, one year following the dividend payment date and subject to continued employment at AnaptysBio,
Inc. or First Tracks Biotherapeutics (as applicable). If the AnaptysBio, Inc. restricted stock unit or option holder is terminated without &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in the applicable equity award agreement) after the dividend is declared but
before any applicable cash payment is made, such payment will be accelerated and paid on the termination date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>AnaptysBio,

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>First Tracks Biotherapeutics 2026 Equity Incentive Plan </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The 2026 Plan, which our named executive officers will participate in, has been filed as an exhibit to the registration statement on Form 10 of
which this information statement forms a part. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Share Awards.</I> The 2026 Plan will provide for the grant of incentive stock options,
or ISOs, nonstatutory stock options, or NSOs, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock awards, restricted stock unit awards, performance-based share awards and other forms of equity compensation, which First Tracks Biotherapeutics refers to
collectively as share awards. Additionally, the 2026 Plan will provide for the grant of performance cash awards. ISOs may be granted only to employees. All other awards may be granted to employees, including officers, and to <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors and consultants of First Tracks Biotherapeutics and its affiliates. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Share
Reserve</I>. At all times First Tracks Biotherapeutics shall reserve and keep available a sufficient number of shares as shall be required to satisfy the requirements of all outstanding awards granted under the 2026 Plan. The 2026 Plan will
initially authorize for issuance up to 4,169,861 shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common shares, and the share reserve will increase automatically on January 1 of each of 2027 through 2036 by the lesser of (i) such number of shares
equal to 5% of the sum of the total number of outstanding shares of all classes of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common stock plus the total number of shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common stock subject to pre-funded warrants
(if any) and the total number of shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common stock issuable upon conversion of any preferred stock (if any), in each case as of the immediately preceding December 31<SUP
STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">st</SUP> or (ii) such other number of shares determined by the First Tracks Biotherapeutics board of directors or compensation committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Reversion of Shares</I>. If a share award granted under the 2026 Plan expires or otherwise terminates without being exercised in full, or
is settled in cash, the common shares not acquired pursuant to the share award again will become available for subsequent issuance under the 2026 Plan. In addition, the following types of shares under the 2026 Plan may become available for the grant
of new share awards under the 2026 Plan: (1)&nbsp;common shares that are forfeited to or repurchased by us prior to becoming fully vested; (2)&nbsp;common shares withheld or reacquired to satisfy income or employment withholding taxes; or
(3)&nbsp;common shares used to pay the exercise or purchase price of a share award. </P>

of 12 months, or (iii) for cause, the optionholder&#8217;s options (whether vested or unvested) will generally expire at such time. In no event may an option be exercised beyond the expiration of its term. </P>

five years from the date of grant. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Restricted Stock Awards</I>. Restricted stock awards will be granted pursuant to restricted stock

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Clawback; Transferability. </I>All awards will be subject to clawback or recoupment pursuant to any compensation clawback or recoupment
policy adopted by our board of directors or required by law, to the extent set forth in such policy or applicable agreement. Except in limited circumstances, awards granted under our 2026 Plan may generally not be transferred in any manner other
than by will or the laws of descent or distribution. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Amendment and Termination</I>. First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; board of
directors will have the authority to amend, suspend, or terminate our 2026 Plan, provided that such action does not materially impair the existing rights of any participant without such participant&#8217;s written consent. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>First Tracks Biotherapeutics 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">First Tracks Biotherapeutics will adopt the 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#8220;ESPP&#8221;). The purpose of the ESPP will be to
secure the services of new employees, to retain the services of existing employees and to provide incentives for such individuals to exert maximum efforts toward First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; success and that of its affiliates. The ESPP will
be intended to qualify as an &#8220;employee stock purchase plan&#8221; within the meaning of Section&nbsp;423 of the Code. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Share
Reserve</I>. The ESPP will authorize the issuance of up to 347,488 shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common shares on a fully diluted basis pursuant to purchase rights granted to our employees or to employees of any of our designated
affiliates. The number of shares reserved for issuance and sale under our ESPP will increase automatically on January 1 of each of 2027 through 2036 by the lesser of (i) such number of shares equal to 1% of the sum of the total number of outstanding
shares of all classes of First Tracks </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Administration</I>. The First Tracks Biotherapeutics compensation committee will have full and exclusive discretionary authority to

Each offering will have one or more purchase dates on which First Tracks Biotherapeutics common shares will be purchased for employees participating in the offering. An offering under the ESPP may be terminated under certain circumstances. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Payroll Deductions</I>. Generally, all regular employees, including executive officers, employed by First Tracks Biotherapeutics or by any
of its designated affiliates, may participate in the ESPP and may contribute, normally through payroll deductions, between 1% and 15% of their earnings (as defined in the ESPP) for the purchase of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common shares
under the ESPP. Unless otherwise determined by First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; board of directors, common shares will be purchased for the accounts of employees participating in the ESPP at a price per share equal to the lower of (a) 85% of the
fair market value of a common share on the first date of an offering or (b) 85% of the fair market value of a common share on the date of purchase. An increase in the rate of payroll deductions may not be made during an offering period unless
otherwise determined by the First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; compensation committee. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Eligibility</I>. Employees may have to satisfy
one or more of the following service requirements before participating in the ESPP, as determined by First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; board of directors, including: (1)&nbsp;being customarily employed for more than 20 hours per week;
(2)&nbsp;being customarily employed for more than five months per calendar year; or (3)&nbsp;continuous employment with First Tracks Biotherapeutics or one of its affiliates for a period of time as specified by the compensation committee. No
employee may purchase shares under the ESPP at a rate in excess of $25,000 worth of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; common shares based on the fair market value per common share at the beginning of an offering for each year such a purchase right
is outstanding. Finally, no employee will be eligible for the grant of any purchase rights under the ESPP if immediately after such rights are granted, such employee has voting power over 5% or more of First Tracks Biotherapeutics&#8217; outstanding
capital stock measured by vote or value pursuant to Section&nbsp;424(d) of the Code. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Changes to Capital Structure</I>. If the number
or class of outstanding First Tracks Biotherapeutics shares is changed by a stock dividend, extraordinary dividend or distribution, recapitalization, stock split, reverse stock split, subdivision, combination, reclassification or similar change in
the capital structure of First Tracks Biotherapeutics, without consideration, then the First Tracks Biotherapeutics compensation committee shall adjust the number and class of common stock that may be delivered under the ESPP, the purchase price and
the number of shares of common stock covered by each option under the ESPP which has not yet been exercised, and the First Tracks Biotherapeutics compensation committee will make appropriate adjustments to (1)&nbsp;the number of shares reserved
under the ESPP, (2)&nbsp;the maximum number of shares by which the share reserve may increase automatically each year, (3)&nbsp;the number of shares and purchase price of all outstanding purchase rights, and (4)&nbsp;the number of shares that are
subject to purchase limits under ongoing offerings. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Corporate Transactions. </I>In the event of any of the following corporate

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AnaptysBio, Inc. sponsors a retirement savings plan established January&nbsp;1, 2007, that is intended to qualify for favorable tax treatment

STYLE="white-space:nowrap">after-tax</FONT> (Roth) salary deferral contributions to the plan from their eligible earnings up to the statutorily prescribed annual limit under the Code. Participants who are 50 years of age or older may contribute
additional amounts based on the statutory limits for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">catch-up</FONT> contributions. Participant contributions are held in trust as required by law. No minimum benefit is provided under the plan. An employee&#8217;s
interest in his or her salary deferral contributions is 100% vested when contributed. AnaptysBio, Inc. has the ability to make discretionary contributions under the plan. It is envisioned that AnaptysBio, Inc&#8217;s 401(k) plan will transfer to
First Tracks Biotherapeutics as part of the distribution. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Other Benefits </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our directors and executive officers may adopt written plans, known as Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10b5-1</FONT> plans, in which they
will contract with a broker to buy or sell our common shares on a periodic basis. Under a Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10b5-1</FONT> plan, a broker executes trades pursuant to parameters established by the director or officer when entering
into the plan, without further direction from them. The director or officer may amend a Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10b5-1</FONT> plan in some circumstances and may terminate a plan at any time. Our directors and executive officers also
may buy or sell additional shares outside of a Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">10b5-1</FONT> plan when they are not in possession of material nonpublic information subject to compliance with the terms of our insider trading policy. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Director Compensation Policy </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Prior to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we will assume the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> director
compensation policy that was previously adopted by AnaptysBio, Inc., which is designed to enable us to attract and retain, on a long-term basis, highly qualified <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> directors. Under the AnaptysBio,

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B><A NAME="tx55540_19"></A>CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Historical Relationship with AnaptysBio, Inc. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On September&nbsp;29, 2025, AnaptysBio, Inc. announced its intention to explore separating its business into two independent, publicly traded
companies. First Tracks Biotherapeutics, Inc. was formed to ultimately hold, directly or indirectly, and conduct certain operational activities in anticipation of the planned separation of the First Tracks Biotherapeutics Business of AnaptysBio,
Inc. Prior to the completion of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we are a wholly owned subsidiary of AnaptysBio, Inc. and all of our outstanding shares of common stock are owned by AnaptysBio, Inc. Upon completion of the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> AnaptysBio, Inc. will own no shares of our common stock. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Since our inception, AnaptysBio,
Inc. has provided certain corporate services to us, and costs associated with these services have been allocated to us in our combined financial statements included elsewhere in this information statement. The allocations include costs of support
functions that are partially provided on a centralized basis by AnaptysBio, Inc. and its affiliates, which include finance, human resources, benefits administration, procurement support, information technology, legal, corporate governance and other
professional services. These costs have been allocated to us based on a specific identification basis or, when specific identification is not practicable, a proportional cost allocation method, primarily based on headcount or other allocation
methodologies that are considered to be a reasonable reflection of the utilization of services provided or the benefit received by us during the periods presented, depending on the nature of the services received. Following the completion of the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we expect to provide AnaptysBio, Inc. and its affiliates certain services related to these functions on a transitional basis to AnaptysBio, Inc. pursuant to the Transition Services Agreement. Upon
completion of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we will assume responsibility for all of our standalone public company costs, including the costs of corporate services provided by AnaptysBio, Inc. and its affiliates to us prior
to the separation. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Agreements to be Entered Into in Connection with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we and AnaptysBio, Inc. will operate separately, each as an independent
publicly traded company. We and AnaptysBio, Inc. will enter into a Separation and Distribution Agreement that will effectuate the separation and distribution. We and AnaptysBio, Inc. will also enter into a Transition Services Agreement. These
agreements will provide a framework for our relationship with AnaptysBio, Inc. after the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> and provide for the allocation between First Tracks Biotherapeutics and AnaptysBio, Inc. of assets, liabilities
and obligations attributable to periods prior to, at and after our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> from AnaptysBio, Inc. The material terms of these agreements will be described in subsequent amendments to this information
statement. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The material agreements between us and AnaptysBio, Inc. are described briefly below and the expected form of such agreements
have been filed as exhibits to the registration statement on Form 10 of which this information statement is a part. These descriptions are subject to, and qualified in their entirety, by reference to the full text of the applicable agreements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Separation and Distribution Agreement </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See the section of this information statement entitled &#8220;<I>The <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off&#8212;The</FONT> Separation and
Distribution Agreement</I>&#8221; above for a description of the Separation and Distribution Agreement. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Transition Services Agreement
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We intend to enter into a Transition Services Agreement pursuant to which we will provide AnaptysBio, Inc., with certain specified
services for a limited time to ensure an orderly transition following the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> The services we will provide will, among others, consist of digital technology, human resources, supply chain, finance, real
estate services and support for AnaptysBio, Inc. to continue to satisfy the contractual requirements of the Vanda Collaboration. The services are generally intended to be provided for a period no longer than two
</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Upon consummation of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> we intend to adopt a written related person transactions policy
providing that our executive officers, directors, nominees for election as a director, beneficial owners of more than 5% of our shares of common stock, and any members of the immediate family of and any entity affiliated with any of the foregoing
persons, are not permitted to enter into a transaction with us in which the amount involved exceeds (i) $120,000 or (ii) 1% of the average of our total assets at <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-end</FONT> for the prior two completed fiscal
years without the review and approval of our audit committee, or a committee composed solely of independent directors in the event it is inappropriate for our audit committee to review such transaction due to a conflict of interest. In approving or
rejecting any such proposal, we expect that our audit committee will consider the relevant facts and circumstances available and deemed relevant to the audit committee, including, but not limited to, whether the transaction is on terms no less
favorable than terms generally available to an unaffiliated third party under the same or similar circumstances and the extent of the related person&#8217;s interest in the transaction. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Agreements with Private Placement Investors </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Purchase Agreement </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On
March 26, 2026, First Tracks Biotherapeutics and the Selling Stockholder entered into the Purchase Agreement with the Private Placement Investors, pursuant to which First Tracks Biotherapeutics agreed to issue and sell an aggregate 5,791,478 shares
of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock, and the Selling Stockholder agreed to sell an aggregate of 4,705,576 shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock that the Selling Stockholder will receive in the Spin-Off to the Private Placement
Investors in the Private Placement, at a purchase price of $13.81 per share. The aggregate gross proceeds to First Tracks Biotherapeutics from the sale of the Primary Shares is expected to be approximately $80&nbsp;million, before deducting offering
expenses. Based on our current plans we believe that our existing cash, cash equivalents and investments will fund our current operating plan beyond the next 12&nbsp;months. First Tracks Biotherapeutics will not receive any proceeds from the sale of
the Secondary Shares. The Private Placement is expected to close subject to, and immediately after, the closing of the Spin-Off. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This section is based on the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the
&#8220;Code&#8221;), its legislative history, existing and proposed regulations, published rulings and court decisions, as well as on applicable tax treaties, all as currently in effect. These authorities are subject to change, possibly on a
retroactive basis. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This discussion is intended to provide only a general summary of the material U.S. federal income tax consequences of
the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> to holders of shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock and the ownership of shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock acquired pursuant to the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> We do not intend it to be a complete analysis or description of all potential U.S. federal income tax consequences of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> The U.S. federal income tax
laws are complex and subject to varying interpretations. Accordingly, the Internal Revenue Service (&#8220;IRS&#8221;) may not agree with the tax consequences described in this information statement. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We have not sought, and do not intend to seek, any ruling from the IRS with respect to the statements made and the conclusions reached in the
following summary, and no assurance can be given that the IRS will agree with the views expressed herein, or that a court will not sustain any challenge by the IRS in the event of litigation. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If an entity or arrangement treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes holds shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock or
shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock, the U.S. federal income tax treatment of a partner will generally depend on the status of the partner and the tax treatment of the partnership. A partner in an entity or arrangement treated as a
partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes holding shares should consult its tax advisors with regard to the U.S. federal income tax treatment of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> and ownership of shares of First Tracks
Biotherapeutics common stock. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> and of the
Ownership and Disposition of Shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics Common Stock to U.S. Holders </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Consequences of the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> to U.S. Holders </I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The distribution of shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock
in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> (including fractional shares for which U.S. holders receive cash) will be treated as a taxable distribution to U.S. holders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. An amount equal to the fair
market value on the Distribution Date of the shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock (including fractional shares for which a U.S. holder receives cash) received by a U.S. holder in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT>
will generally be treated as a taxable dividend to the extent of such holder&#8217;s ratable share of any current or accumulated earnings and profits of AnaptysBio, Inc. (including gain recognized by AnaptysBio, Inc. in connection with the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off),</FONT> with the excess treated first as a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-taxable</FONT> return of capital to the extent of such holder&#8217;s tax basis in shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock and any
remaining excess treated as capital gain. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Dividends will be taxed as ordinary income to the extent that they are paid out of AnaptysBio,
Inc.&#8217;s current or accumulated earnings and profits. Dividends paid to a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-corporate</FONT> U.S. holder that constitute qualified dividend income are taxable to the stockholder at the preferential rates
applicable to long-term capital gains, provided that the stockholder holds the shares for more than 60 days during the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">121-day</FONT> period beginning 60 days before the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">ex-dividend</FONT> date and meets other holding period requirements. AnaptysBio, Inc. expects that any amount treated as a dividend paid by AnaptysBio, Inc. pursuant to the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> will constitute qualified dividend income, assuming the U.S. holder&#8217;s holding period requirements are met. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A U.S. holder&#8217;s tax basis in its shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock held on the Distribution Date will be reduced (but not below
zero) to the extent that the fair market value on the Distribution Date of the shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock received by such U.S. holder from AnaptysBio, Inc. in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> exceeds
such U.S. holder&#8217;s ratable share of AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s current and accumulated earnings and profits (that is, the amount treated as a taxable dividend). AnaptysBio, Inc. has not calculated earnings and profits in accordance with U.S.
federal income tax principles. Accordingly, U.S. holders should expect to treat the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> as a taxable dividend for U.S. federal income tax purposes. </P>

Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock received by a U.S. holder from AnaptysBio, Inc. in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> exceeds such U.S. holder&#8217;s adjusted tax basis in its shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock, the U.S.
holder generally must include such excess in income as long-term capital gain, or short-term capital gain if the U.S. holder&#8217;s shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock have been held for one year or less. A U.S. holder&#8217;s holding period
for its AnaptysBio, Inc. shares will not be affected by the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A U.S. holder&#8217;s tax
basis in the shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock received in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> generally will equal the fair market value of those shares on the Distribution Date, and a U.S. holder&#8217;s holding
period for those shares will begin the day after the Distribution Date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Although AnaptysBio, Inc. will ascribe a value to the shares of
First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock it distributes in the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> for tax purposes, this valuation is not binding on the IRS or any other tax authority. These taxing authorities could ascribe a higher
valuation to those shares, particularly if shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock trade at prices significantly above the value ascribed to those shares by AnaptysBio, Inc. in the period following the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off.</FONT> Such a higher valuation may cause a larger reduction in the tax basis of a U.S. holder&#8217;s shares of AnaptysBio, Inc. common stock or may cause a U.S. holder to recognize additional dividend or
capital gain income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Distributions on Shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics Common Stock </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As described in the section entitled &#8220;<I>Dividend Policy</I>,&#8221; we do not anticipate declaring or paying cash dividends to holders
of shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock in the foreseeable future. However, if we do make distributions of cash or property on shares of our common stock, such distributions will constitute dividends for U.S. federal income tax
purposes to the extent paid from our current or accumulated earnings and profits, as determined under U.S. federal income tax principles. Dividends received by certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-corporate</FONT> U.S. holders (including
individuals) may be taxed at preferential rates applicable to qualified dividend income, provided certain holding period requirements are met. Corporate U.S. holders that meet certain holding period and other requirements may be eligible for a
dividends-received deduction for a portion of the dividend received. Amounts not treated as dividends for U.S. federal income tax purposes will constitute a return of capital and first be applied against and reduce a U.S. holder&#8217;s adjusted tax
basis in its shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock, but not below zero. Any excess will be treated as capital gain. Such gain generally will be taxable as long-term capital gain if the shares have been held for more than one year. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Sale or Other Taxable Disposition of Shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics Common Stock </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Upon a subsequent sale or other taxable disposition of a share of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock, a U.S. holder will recognize
taxable gain or loss equal to the difference between the amount realized on the disposition of the share and the U.S. holder&#8217;s tax basis in the share. The gain or loss will be capital gain or loss. A
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-corporate</FONT> U.S. holder, including an individual, who has held the share for more than one year generally will be eligible for reduced tax rates for such long-term capital gains. The deductibility of capital
losses is subject to limitations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> and of
the Ownership and Disposition of Shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics Common Stock to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Holders </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Consequences of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Holders
</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> holders will be treated
as receiving a distribution from AnaptysBio, Inc. in an amount equal to the fair market value on the Distribution Date of the shares of First Tracks Biotherapeutics common stock (including fractional shares for which a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> holder receives cash), which will be treated as a dividend to the extent the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Spin-Off</FONT> is paid out of AnaptysBio, Inc.&#8217;s current or accumulated earnings
and profits (as determined under U.S. federal income tax principles). Distributions in excess of current and accumulated </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">148 </P>
